One correction to the reviewer's rationale, which I could not substantiate: the phrase "3px bar as the only marker of the current page" is their gloss, not the design's — no such copy exists anywhere in the canvas (grep for "only marker", "3px bar", "only signal", "colour alone" returns nothing), and the active state is not colour-only in any case: `.sb-link--on { background:rgba(255,255,255,.1); color:#fff; }` plus `.sb-link--on svg { color:var(--brick-400); }` add a tint, white label, and recoloured icon alongside the bar. The 1.4.11 consequence is also weaker than stated: the true 4.03:1 comfortably clears the 3:1 non-text threshold, so nothing actually fails — the defect is a mis-attributed usage and an unpublished ratio, not an accessibility failure. Verdict: the wrong-fact finding holds on its evidence (wrong token, wrong hex, wrong backdrop, wrong ratio for that one use), but severity should drop from the implied 1.4.11-blocker framing to a minor documentation error.
